Metadata.description: A free, privacy-first training dashboard for triathletes. Your training, finally clear.

hero.title: Your training, finally clear.
hero.subtitle: Connect Strava and see your swim, bike, run and strength training the way it should be shown: a clear calendar, weekly totals, your best efforts and goals. Free, and only for your eyes.

privacy.title: Your data stays yours
privacy.onlyYou: Only you can see your data. No feeds, no leaderboards, no public profiles.
privacy.noAds: No ads, no data selling and no AI training on your data.
privacy.control: Export or permanently delete everything at any time.

cta.title: See your own training like this
cta.text: Free, private and made for triathletes. Connecting Strava takes a minute.

video.title: Stramin in 30 seconds
video.text: From Strava to your calendar, goals, pace calculator and progress.

Guide.title: Import your Garmin history
Guide.intro: Garmin only sends new activities to Stramin. To see your full history, download a copy of your data from Garmin once and upload it to Stramin.

open.title: Open your Garmin account
open.text: Log in to your Garmin account and go to data management.

request.title: Request your data
request.text: Click "Export Your Data" and then "Request Data Export".

wait.title: Wait for the email
wait.text: Garmin sends you an email with a download link. It usually takes about 48 hours, but can take up to 30 days.

download.title: Download the file
download.text: Open the link in the email and download the ZIP file. Don't unzip it.

upload.title: Upload it to Stramin
upload.text: Upload the whole ZIP file to Stramin. Coming soon.

Guide.note: You only need to do this once. After that, new activities arrive automatically through the Garmin connection.

cruise-intervals.description: Threshold running in blocks: raises the pace you can hold.

bike-endurance.name: Endurance ride

bike-tempo.name: Tempo 3 × 12 min
bike-tempo.description: Long tempo efforts that build race-day strength.

bike-vo2.name: VO2max 5 × 4 min
bike-vo2.description: Hard efforts that raise your ceiling.

swim-technique.name: Technique swim

swim-aerobic.description: Steady, longer repeats that build swim endurance.

bike-recovery.name: Recovery spin

tips.speedLimit: Your {reference} ({best}) is slower than this goal needs (about {needed}). Speed comes first.
tips.enduranceLimit: Your {reference} is already fast enough. Build endurance to hold the pace for longer.
tips.workout5k: Key session: 5–6 × 1 km at about {pace}, with 2–3 minutes easy between.
tips.workoutHalf: Key session: 3 × 10 minutes at about {pace} (threshold), and a long run every week.
tips.workoutMarathon: Key session: long runs with 2 × 20 minutes at goal pace ({pace}).
tips.fuelRun: Practise taking energy every 30–45 minutes on your long runs.
tips.workoutBikeShort: Key session: 2 × 20 minutes close to your threshold. Goal speed: {speed}.
tips.workoutBikeLong: Key session: one long ride a week at an easy, even effort (zone 2).
tips.fuelBike: Practise eating and drinking on the bike: about 60 g of carbs an hour.
tips.workoutSwim: Key session: 10 × 100 m at about {pace}, 15 s rest.
tips.technique: Spend one swim a week on technique (e.g. catch-up and single-arm drills).
tips.openWater: Practise in open water with a wetsuit: sighting and the start cost time.
tips.gapClose: Close. A few focused weeks can do it.
tips.gapBig: A big step. Aim for {time} first.
tips.easy: Keep about 80 % of your training easy, so you can go hard when it counts.
tips.recoveryWeek: Add at most about 10 % a week, and take an easier week every 3–4 weeks.
tips.workoutBikeShortWatts: Key session: 2 × 20 minutes at about {low}–{high} W (close to your threshold). Goal speed: {speed}.
tips.workoutBikeLongWatts: Key session: one long ride a week at about {low}–{high} W (zone 2).
tips.freshNeeded: {sport}: when fresh, you should manage about {time} over {distance} ({pace}).
